Multiplier Ideals, V-filtrations and Transversal Sections

A. Dimca Address:  Laboratoire J.A. Dieudonné, UMR du CNRS 6621, Université de Nice-Sophia Antipolis, Parc Valrose, 06108 Nice Cedex 02, FRANCE. Email address: dimca@math.unice.fr , Ph. Maisonobe Address:  Laboratoire J.A. Dieudonné, UMR du CNRS 6621, Université de Nice-Sophia Antipolis, Parc Valrose, 06108 Nice Cedex 02, FRANCE. Email address: phm@math.unice.fr , M. Saito Address:  RIMS Kyoto University, Kyoto 606–8502 JAPAN Email address: msaito@kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp and T. Torrelli Address:  Laboratoire J.A. Dieudonné, UMR du CNRS 6621, Université de Nice-Sophia Antipolis, Parc Valrose, 06108 Nice Cedex 02, FRANCE. Email address: torrelli@math.unice.fr
Abstract.

We show that the restriction to a smooth transversal section commutes to the computation of multiplier ideals and V-filtrations. As an application we prove the constancy of the spectrum along any stratum of a Whitney regular stratification.

Key words and phrases: 
multipler ideal, V-filtration, spectrum, Whitney regular stratification
2000 Mathematics Subject Classification
Primary 14B05, 32S35; Secondary 32S30, 32S40, 32S60.

1. Introduction

Let XX be a complex nn-dimensional manifold and D⊂XD\subset X an effective divisor defined by a holomorphic function ff. To put the results of this paper in their proper perspective, we start by recalling the local topological triviality of Whitney regular stratifications, see for details [9], [12].

If 𝒮{\mathcal{S}} is a Whitney regular stratification of the reduced divisor Dr​e​dD_{red} and x0∈Dx_{0}\in D belongs to a (connected) stratum S∈𝒮S\in{\mathcal{S}} with d=dimS>0d=\dim S>0, then the local topology of the pair (X,D)(X,D) at the point x0x_{0} is given by the product (T,T∩D)×(S,0)(T,T\cap D)\times(S,0), where (T,x0)(T,x_{0}) is a smooth transversal to SS at x0x_{0}, i.e. dimT=n−d\dim T=n-d and T⋔ST\pitchfork S. In other words, the local topology of the pair (X,D)(X,D) is constant along the stratum SS.

In terms of constructible sheaves, the topology of the pair (X,D)(X,D) is described by the vanishing cycle sheaf complex ϕf​(ℚX)∈Dcb​(ℚD)\phi_{f}(\mathbb{Q}_{X})\in D_{c}^{b}(\mathbb{Q}_{D}), see for instance [10]. If iT:T→Xi_{T}:T\to X denotes the inclusion of the transversal TT above, then there is an isomorphism

(1.1) ϕf∘iT​(ℚT)=iT−1​ϕf​(ℚX)\phi_{f\circ i_{T}}(\mathbb{Q}_{T})=i_{T}^{-1}\phi_{f}(\mathbb{Q}_{X})

in the derived category Dcb​(ℚT∩D)D_{c}^{b}(\mathbb{Q}_{T\cap D}), see for instance [38], Lemma 4.3.4, p. 265. In fact this isomorphism holds for any 𝒮{\mathcal{S}}-constructible complex 𝒞∈Dcb​(ℚX){\mathcal{C}}\in D_{c}^{b}(\mathbb{Q}_{X}), namely

(1.2) ϕf∘iT​(iT−1​𝒞)=iT−1​ϕf​(𝒞).\phi_{f\circ i_{T}}(i_{T}^{-1}{\mathcal{C}})=i_{T}^{-1}\phi_{f}({\mathcal{C}}).

This more general view-point allows us, in particular, to reduce the case of an arbitrary divisor DD to the case of a smooth hypersurface HH, via the following basic construction. Set X′=X×ℂX^{\prime}=X\times\mathbb{C} and let if:X→X′i_{f}:X\to X^{\prime} be the graph embedding x↦(x,f⁡(x))x\mapsto(x,f(x)). If tt denotes the coordinate on ℂ\mathbb{C}, then one has

(1.3) ϕt(if∗𝒞)=if∗ϕf(𝒞).\phi_{t}(i_{f*}{\mathcal{C}})=i_{f*}\phi_{f}({\mathcal{C}}).

Indeed, ifi_{f} is proper and ϕf\phi_{f} commutes with proper direct images, see for instance [10], p. 109.

In this paper we prove two analogs of the above well-known properties.

Theorem 1.1.

Let D:f=0D:f=0 be a smooth divisor in XX and let iT:T→Xi_{T}:T\to X be the inclusion of a closed submanifold which is transversal to DD. Assume that MM is a regular holonomic 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X}-module such that TT is non-characteristic for MM and for M(∗D)M(*D). Let VV denote the Kashiwara-Malgrange filtration of MM along the hypersurface DD and also the Kashiwara-Malgrange filtration of the restriction iT∗​Mi_{T}^{*}M along the hypersurface T∩DT\cap D. Then, for any α∈ℂ\alpha\in\mathbb{C}, the following hold:

(i) iT∗​(Vα​M)=Vα​iT∗​Mi_{T}^{*}(V^{\alpha}M)=V^{\alpha}i_{T}^{*}M;   (ii) iT∗​(G​rVα​M)=G​rVα​iT∗​Mi_{T}^{*}(Gr_{V}^{\alpha}M)=Gr_{V}^{\alpha}i_{T}^{*}M.

In particular, iT∗​(ψf​M)=ψf|T​(iT∗​M)i_{T}^{*}(\psi_{f}M)=\psi_{f|T}(i_{T}^{*}M) and iT∗​(ϕf​M)=ϕf|T​(iT∗​M)i_{T}^{*}(\phi_{f}M)=\phi_{f|T}(i_{T}^{*}M).

For more details on the notions involved in this theorem we refer the reader to the next section. We mention here that the non-characteristic condition is a generalization of the transversality condition used in (1.1) and (1.2) which implies that the analytic pull-back iT∗​(M)i_{T}^{*}(M) coincides with the left derived pull-back 𝕃​iT∗​(M)\mathbb{L}i_{T}^{*}(M), see Proposition 2.5. Moreover, the V-filtration is the necessary ingredient to construct a theory of vanishing cycles for the regular holonomic 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X}-modules, see [29], [18], [32], [26] for a synthesis. For other applications of Theorem 1.1 to the monodromy and Bernstein polynomials of families of hypersurface singularities, see [28].

To state the second result, we return to the general case, i.e. DD is an effective divisor on XX defined by a holomorphic function ff. The family of multiplier ideals {ℐ⁡(α​D)}α∈ℚ\{{\mathcal{I}}(\alpha D)\}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{Q}} associated to DD is a decreasing family of ideals in the structure sheaf 𝒪X{\mathcal{O}}_{X} which encodes a lot of the algebraic geometry of the pair (X,D)(X,D), see [8], [22], [23] for more on this beautiful and very active subject. Using the deep relation between multiplier ideals and V-filtrations established in [7] and Theorem 1.1 above, we obtain the following.

Theorem 1.2.

Assume TT is transversal to any stratum of a Whitney regular stratification of the reduced divisor Dr​e​dD_{red}, or more generally, TT is non-characteristic for the regular holonomic 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X}-module 𝒪X(∗D){\mathcal{O}}_{X}(*D). Then for α∈ℚ\alpha\in\mathbb{Q}, we have a canonical isomorphism

iT∗​ℐ​(α​D)=ℐ⁡(α⁡(D∩T)),i_{T}^{*}{\mathcal{I}}(\alpha D)={\mathcal{I}}(\alpha(D\cap T)),

compatible with the inclusions ℐ⁡(α​D)→ℐ⁡(α′​D){\mathcal{I}}(\alpha D)\to{\mathcal{I}}(\alpha^{\prime}D) and ℐ⁡(α⁡(D∩T))→ℐ⁡(α′​(D∩T)){\mathcal{I}}(\alpha(D\cap T))\to{\mathcal{I}}(\alpha^{\prime}(D\cap T)) for α>α′\alpha>\alpha^{\prime}, where the isomorphism for α≤0\alpha\leq 0 is the natural isomorphism iT∗​𝒪X=𝒪Ti_{T}^{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}={\mathcal{O}}_{T}.

Note that the multiplier ideals ℐ⁡(α​D){\mathcal{I}}(\alpha D) are essentially given by the filtration 𝒥⁡(α){\mathcal{J}}(\alpha) on 𝒪X=𝒪X⊗1{\mathcal{O}}_{X}={\mathcal{O}}_{X}\otimes 1 induced by the V-filtration on the 𝒟X′{\mathcal{D}}_{X^{\prime}}-module Bf:=if+𝒪X=𝒪X⊗ℂ[∂t]B_{f}:=i_{f+}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}={\mathcal{O}}_{X}\otimes\mathbb{C}[\partial_{t}] along the smooth hypersurface H:t=0H:t=0, see [7]. Here if+i_{f+} denotes the direct image as a 𝒟{\mathcal{D}}-module. Therefore Theorem 1.2 is not a straightforward consequence of Theorem 1.1 above. We can generalize Theorem 1.2 to the case of arbitrary subvarieties (see 5.3). From Theorem 1.2 we can deduce the following application to the spectrum in the sense of J. Steenbrink [39] (see (4.4-5)):

Corollary 1.3.

Under the assumption of Theorem 1.2, the spectrum Sp⁡(f,x)\Sp(f,x) of ff at x∈Tx\in T coincides with Sp⁡(f|T,x)\Sp(f|_{T},x) up to a sign. In particular, Sp⁡(f|T,x)\Sp(f|_{T},x) is independent of TT in Theorem 1.2.

It has been known that the spectrum is constant under a μ\mu-constant deformation of isolated hypersurface singularities, see [41]. We have a weak generalization as follows.

Corollary 1.4.

Let SS be a (connected) stratum of a Whitney regular stratification of Dr​e​dD_{red}. Then Sp⁡(f,x)\Sp(f,x) and Sp⁡(f|T,x)\Sp(f|_{T},x) are independent of x∈Sx\in S, where TT is transversal to SS at xx.

Note that the μ\mu-constantness is equivalent to the Thom afa_{f}-condition (see [25] and 4.8 below) and the latter is weaker than the Whitney (b)(b) condition, see [4]. It is not clear whether Corollary 1.4 holds assuming only the afa_{f}-condition without the Whitney (b)(b) condition.

2. Basic facts on 𝒟{\mathcal{D}}-modules

2.1. Non-characteristic inverse images

Let XX be a complex nn-dimensional manifold and denote by T∗​XT^{*}X its cotangent bundle. A point (x,ξ)∈T∗​X(x,\xi)\in T^{*}X is just a pair formed by a point x∈Xx\in X and a linear form ξ:Tx​X→ℂ\xi:T_{x}X\to\mathbb{C}, where Tx​XT_{x}X denotes the tangent space to XX at the point xx. When Z⊂XZ\subset X is a locally closed analytic subset of XX, we denote by TZ∗​XT^{*}_{Z}X the conormal space of ZZ in XX. This is by definition the closure in T∗​X|Z:=π−1​(Z)T^{*}X|Z:=\pi^{-1}(Z), with π:T∗​X→X\pi:T^{*}X\to X the canonical projection, of the set of pairs (x,ξ)∈T∗​X(x,\xi)\in T^{*}X with x∈Zx\in Z a smooth point on ZZ and ξ|Tx​Z=0\xi|T_{x}Z=0. In particular, TX∗​XT^{*}_{X}X is just the zero section of the cotangent bundle.

Definition 2.2.

Let MM be a coherent 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X}-module and let C​V​(M)⊂T∗​XCV(M)\subset T^{*}X be its characteristic variety. A submanifold Z⊂XZ\subset X is non characteristic for MM if

C​V​(M)∩TZ∗​X⊂TX∗​X.CV(M)\cap T^{*}_{Z}X\subset T^{*}_{X}X.

The following basic example explains the relation to the transversality discussed briefly in the Introduction.

Example 2.3.

The Riemann-Hilbert correspondence, see [31],[19], says that the DR-functor establishes an equivalence of categories

D​R:Dr​hb​(𝒟X)→Dcb​(ℂX)DR:D_{rh}^{b}({\mathcal{D}}_{X})\to D_{c}^{b}(\mathbb{C}_{X})

such that, for a regular holonomic 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X}-module MM, the sheaf complex ℱ=D​R​(M){\mathcal{F}}=DR(M) is a perverse sheaf. Moreover, the characteristic variety C​V​(M)CV(M) coincides to the characteristic variety C​V​(ℱ)CV({\mathcal{F}}), which is defined topologically, see for instance [21] or [10], p. 111–113. If 𝒮{\mathcal{S}} is a Whitney regular stratification of XX such that ℱ{\mathcal{F}} is 𝒮{\mathcal{S}}-constructible, then

CV(ℱ)⊂∪S∈𝒮TS∗XCV({\mathcal{F}})\subset\cup_{S\in{\mathcal{S}}}T_{S}^{*}X

see for instance [10], p. 119. It follows that a submanifold TT which is transversal to 𝒮{\mathcal{S}}, i.e. it is transversal to all the strata S∈𝒮S\in{\mathcal{S}}, it is automatically non-characteristic for MM. Note that transversality of TT to a single stratum SS at a point x∈Sx\in S implies, via the (a)-regularity condition, transversality to all strata in a small neighborhood of xx in XX.

To be even more specific, when M=𝒪X(∗D)M={\mathcal{O}}_{X}(*D), then DR(𝒪X(∗D))=Rj∗ℂU[n]DR({\mathcal{O}}_{X}(*D))=Rj_{*}\mathbb{C}_{U}[n], where U=X∖DU=X\setminus D and j:U→Xj:U\to X is the inclusion, see [14], [33]. If 𝒮{\mathcal{S}} is a Whitney regular stratification of DD, then consider the Whitney regular stratification of XX given by 𝒮0=𝒮∪{U}{\mathcal{S}}_{0}={\mathcal{S}}\cup\{U\}. It follows that R​j∗​ℂU​[n]Rj_{*}\mathbb{C}_{U}[n] is 𝒮0{\mathcal{S}}_{0}-constructible and hence, if TT is transversal to 𝒮{\mathcal{S}} as above, then TT is non-characteristic for 𝒪X(∗D){\mathcal{O}}_{X}(*D).

The following result tells us that the property of being non-characteristic is preserved under small deformations.

Lemma 2.4.

Let MM be a holonomic 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X}-module and T⊂XT\subset X a submanifold which is non-characteristic for MM. Let a∈Ta\in T be any point in TT and p:(X,a)→(S,0)p:(X,a)\to(S,0) be the germ of a submersion onto a smooth germ (S,0)(S,0) such that the space germ induced by the special fiber p−1​(0)p^{-1}(0) coincides to (T,a)(T,a). Then there is an open neighborhood UU of aa in XX on which pp is defined and such that all the fibers p−1​(s)∩Up^{-1}(s)\cap U for s∈Ss\in S are non-characteristic for the 𝒟U{\mathcal{D}}_{U}-module M|UM|U.

Proof.

Since the question is local on XX, we may suppose that X=S×TX=S\times T and pp is the first projection. On the other hand, it is known that the characteristic variety of a holonomic 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X}-module MM has the following local decomposition

(2.1) CV(M)=∪j=1,mTZj∗XCV(M)=\cup_{j=1,m}T^{*}_{Z_{j}}X

where ZjZ_{j} are closed irreducible analytic subsets in XX and the conormal spaces TZj∗​XT^{*}_{Z_{j}}X are exactly the irreducible components of the characteristic variety C​V​(M)CV(M). If a neighborhood UU as claimed above does not exist, then there is an index jj and a sequence of points an∈Xa_{n}\in X such that

(i) an→aa_{n}\to a;

(ii) for each nn, there is a point (an,ξn)∈TZj∗​X(a_{n},\xi_{n})\in T^{*}_{Z_{j}}X such that ξn≠0\xi_{n}\neq 0 and ξn|0×Tq⁡(an)​T=0\xi_{n}|0\times T_{q(a_{n})}T=0, where q:S×T→Tq:S\times T\to T is the second projection.

Moreover, we can norm the linear form ξn\xi_{n}, e.g. by dividing by their norm and passing to a convergent subsequence, such that we may assume that

(iii) ξn→ξ≠0\xi_{n}\to\xi\neq 0.

Since TZj∗​XT^{*}_{Z_{j}}X is a closed subset, it follows that (a,ξ)=lim(an,ξn)∈TZj∗​X(a,\xi)=\lim(a_{n},\xi_{n})\in T^{*}_{Z_{j}}X. From (ii) we infer that ξ|0×Tq⁡(a)​T=0\xi|0\times T_{q(a)}T=0. Therefore (a,ξ)∈TT∗​X∩C​V​(M)(a,\xi)\in T^{*}_{T}X\cap CV(M), in contradiction to the fact that TT is non-characteristic for MM.

∎

We recall now the following result on non-characteristic inverse images, see for instance [17] or [27], Prop. II.1.3, Thm. II.1.7.

Proposition 2.5.

Let TT be a submanifold in XX given by global equations z1=…=zc=0z_{1}=...=z_{c}=0, where c=codim⁡Tc=\codim T such that TT is non-characteristic for a coherent 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X}-module MM. If iT:T→Xi_{T}:T\to X is the closed inclusion of TT into XX, then the derived inverse image complex iT+​M=𝕃​iT∗​Mi_{T}^{+}M=\mathbb{L}i_{T}^{*}M is concentrated in degree zero and coincides to the coherent 𝒟T{\mathcal{D}}_{T}-module

iT∗​M=iT−1​Mz1​iT−1​M+…+zc​iT−1​M.i_{T}^{*}M=\frac{i^{-1}_{T}M}{z_{1}i^{-1}_{T}M+...+z_{c}i^{-1}_{T}M}.

Moreover, z1,…,zcz_{1},...,z_{c} is a regular sequence in iT−1​M{i^{-1}_{T}M} and iT∗​Mi_{T}^{*}M is holonomic when MM is holonomic. More precisely, in this last situation, if CV(M)=∪j=1,mTZj∗XCV(M)=\cup_{j=1,m}T^{*}_{Z_{j}}X, then

CV(iT∗M)=∪j=1,mTT∩Zj∗T.CV(i_{T}^{*}M)=\cup_{j=1,m}T^{*}_{T\cap Z_{j}}T.

The idea of the proof of this result is to determine the characteristic variety C​V​(iT∗​M)CV(i_{T}^{*}M), see Thm. II.1.7 in [27]. In the proof of Prop. II.1.3 in [27] it is shown that 𝕃​iT∗​M\mathbb{L}i_{T}^{*}M is represented by the Koszul complex of the sequence z1,…,zcz_{1},...,z_{c} in MM. Then this sequence is shown to be regular, by showing that any local section germ in MM is killed by some special type differential operators, similar to the ones we construct below in Lemma 3.2. See also Corollary I.3.3 in [27]. It follows that the Koszul complex has non-trivial homology only in degree zero, which yields the result.

2.6. V-filtrations, b-polynomials and vanishing cycles

Let XX be a complex analytic manifold and H⊂XH\subset X a smooth hypersurface. Let ℐ{\mathcal{I}} be the ideal sheaf defining HH. We define the decreasing Kashiwara-Malgrange V-filtration of 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X} along HH by setting, for k∈ℤk\in\mathbb{Z},

(2.2) Vk​(𝒟X)={P∈𝒟X|P⁡(ℐj)⊂ℐj+k​ for all ​j∈ℤ}V^{k}({\mathcal{D}}_{X})=\{P\in{\mathcal{D}}_{X}~|~P({\mathcal{I}}^{j})\subset{\mathcal{I}}^{j+k}\text{ for all }j\in\mathbb{Z}\}

where ℐj=𝒪X{\mathcal{I}}^{j}={\mathcal{O}}_{X} for any j<0j<0. It is easy to check that Vk​(𝒟X)⋅Vℓ​(𝒟X)⊂Vk+ℓ​(𝒟X)V^{k}({\mathcal{D}}_{X})\cdot V^{\ell}({\mathcal{D}}_{X})\subset V^{k+\ell}({\mathcal{D}}_{X}). In particular, V0​(𝒟X)V^{0}({\mathcal{D}}_{X}) is a coherent sheaf of rings, see [26], Prop. 2.1.5.

If t=0t=0 is a local equation for HH, then the differential operator t∂tt\partial_{t} induces an element EE in G​rV0​𝒟X=V0​(𝒟X)/V1​(𝒟X)Gr^{0}_{V}{\mathcal{D}}_{X}=V^{0}({\mathcal{D}}_{X})/V^{1}({\mathcal{D}}_{X}). This is called the Euler operator of HH and it is independent of the choice of the local equation t=0t=0.

A coherent 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X}-module MM is said to be specializable along the hypersurface HH if it satisfies the following condition:

(⋆\star) For any point x∈Hx\in H and any germ m∈Mxm\in M_{x}, there is a non zero polynomial b⁡(s)∈ℂ⁡[s]b(s)\in\mathbb{C}[s] such that b⁡(E+1)​m∈V1​(𝒟X)x​mb(E+1)m\in V^{1}({\mathcal{D}}_{X})_{x}m.

For more details, see [26], Propositions II.1.9, II.2.2 and II.2.4. It is known that a holonomic 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X}-module is specializable along any smooth hypersurface, see [18]. The Bernstein polynomial (or the b-function) bmb_{m} of the germ m∈Mxm\in M_{x} is the unitary polynomial of minimal degree satisfying the condition (⋆\star). Note that E+1=∂t⋅tE+1=\partial_{t}\cdot t. This shift by 1 is justified by the formula (2.3) below.

Let << be a total order on ℂ\mathbb{C} such that, for any u,v∈ℂu,v\in\mathbb{C} we have u<u+1u<u+1, u<vu<v if and only if u+1<v+1u+1<v+1 and, finally, there is some m∈ℕm\in\mathbb{N} such that v<u+mv<u+m. For instance, we can take the lexicografic order on ℂ=ℝ2\mathbb{C}=\mathbb{R}^{2}. Using this order, we define the decreasing Kashiwara-Malgrange V-filtration along HH on the coherent 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X}-module MM, assumed to be specializable along HH, by

(2.3) Vα​Mx={m∈Mx| all the roots of the b-function​bm​are≥α}.V^{\alpha}M_{x}=\{m\in M_{x}~|~\text{ all the roots of the $b$-function}~~b_{m}~~\text{are}~\geq\alpha\}.

See Kashiwara [18], Malgrange [29], and also [34]. The filtration Vα​MV^{\alpha}M is indexed by a finite union of lattices β+ℤ\beta+\mathbb{Z} in ℂ\mathbb{C}, hence it is a discrete, decreasing and exhaustive filtration on MM. In most cases coming from geometry, e.g. when MM is obtained by applying some natural functors to the 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X}-module 𝒪X{\mathcal{O}}_{X}, then all β∈ℚ\beta\in\mathbb{Q}, and hence VV is actually indexed by ℚ\mathbb{Q}. This is the case in particular for the module M=BfM=B_{f}.

It turns out that the V-filtration can be defined by the following list of characteristic properties, see [34], [37] for more details. Define V>αM=∪β>αVβMV^{>\alpha}M=\cup_{\beta>\alpha}V^{\beta}M and G​rVα​M=Vα​M/V>α​MGr_{V}^{\alpha}M=V^{\alpha}M/V^{>\alpha}M.

Proposition 2.7.

Let MM be a coherent 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X}-module, specializable along HH. The Kashiwara-Malgrange V-filtration is the unique discrete, decreasing and exhaustive filtration on MM satisfying the following conditions:

  1. (1)

    Vk​(𝒟X)⋅Vα​M⊂Vk+α​MV^{k}({\mathcal{D}}_{X})\cdot V^{\alpha}M\subset V^{k+\alpha}M, for any k∈ℤk\in\mathbb{Z} and α∈ℂ\alpha\in\mathbb{C};

    Vα​MV^{\alpha}M is a coherent V0​(𝒟X)V^{0}({\mathcal{D}}_{X})-module, for any α∈ℂ\alpha\in\mathbb{C};

    t⋅Vα​M=Vα+1​Mt\cdot V^{\alpha}M=V^{\alpha+1}M, for α>>0\alpha>>0;

    the action of ∂t⋅t−α\partial_{t}\cdot t-\alpha on G​rVα​MGr_{V}^{\alpha}M is locally nilpotent.

Remark 2.8.

Many authors prefer to work with the increasing V-filtration defined by Vα​M=V−α​MV_{\alpha}M=V^{-\alpha}M, see for instance [26]. Our choice here is justified by the fact that, as we mentioned in the Introduction, in an important case the V-filtration is essentially the filtration induced by the family of multiplier ideals, which is by definition a decreasing filtration.

2.10. Relatively specializable 𝒟X{\mathcal{D}}_{X}-modules and relative V-filtrations

In the situation of the previous subsection, suppose that we have in addition a submersion p:X→Sp:X\to S such that the composition pH=p∘iHp_{H}=p\circ i_{H} is still a submersion. A coherent 𝒟X/S{\mathcal{D}}_{X/S}-module MM is relatively specializable along HH if there exists a decreasing, exhaustive filtration Uk​(M)k∈ℤU^{k}(M)_{k\in\mathbb{Z}} of MM by coherent V0​(𝒟X/S)V^{0}({\mathcal{D}}_{X/S})-submodules such that the following conditions are satisfied:

For more details, see [28]. Moreover, the converse implication is easy to check. In the following, we will use this last characterization.

where ℳi=Fp0​Vα−i​M|Z{\mathcal{M}}^{i}=F_{p_{0}}V^{\alpha-i}M|_{Z}. This is further reduced to the surjectivity of the action of t∂t−i0t\partial_{t}-i_{0} on

∏i≠i0(ℳxi⊗ti)​⋂ℳx∼.\hbox{$\prod_{i\neq i_{0}}({\mathcal{M}}^{i}_{x}\otimes t^{i})\bigcap{\mathcal{M}}^{\sim}_{x}$}.

Here ℳx∼{\mathcal{M}}^{\sim}_{x} is viewed as a completion of ℳx{\mathcal{M}}_{x} in some topology, and is identified with a vector subspace of ∏i(ℳxi⊗ti)\prod_{i}({\mathcal{M}}^{i}_{x}\otimes t^{i}). This surjectivity is reduced to the case ℳ=𝒜{\mathcal{M}}={\mathcal{A}} and ℳ∼=𝒪𝒳|Z{\mathcal{M}}^{\sim}={\mathcal{O}}_{{\mathcal{X}}}|_{Z} taking homogeneous generators vjv_{j} of ℳx{\mathcal{M}}_{x} (i.e. vj∈ℳxij⊗tijv_{j}\in{\mathcal{M}}_{x}^{i_{j}}\otimes t^{i_{j}}). For ℳ=𝒜{\mathcal{M}}={\mathcal{A}} we take local coordinate system (x1′,…,xn′,y1′,…,yr′,t′)(x^{\prime}_{1},\dots,x^{\prime}_{n};y^{\prime}_{1},\dots,y^{\prime}_{r};t^{\prime}) of 𝒳{\mathcal{X}} which is related to a local coordinate system (x1,…,xn,y1,…,yr,t)(x_{1},\dots,x_{n};y_{1},\dots,y_{r};t) of X×ℂr×ℂX\times\mathbb{C}^{r}\times\mathbb{C} by xi=xi′,yj=yj′​t′,t=t′x_{i}=x^{\prime}_{i},y_{j}=y^{\prime}_{j}t^{\prime},t=t^{\prime}. Then the vector field t∂tt\partial_{t} on 𝒳{\mathcal{X}} is expressed by t′∂t′−∑jy′j∂yj′t^{\prime}\partial_{t^{\prime}}-\sum_{j}y^{\prime}_{j}\partial_{y^{\prime}_{j}}, and we can prove the surjectivity using the grading of ℂ⁡{x′,y′,t′}\mathbb{C}\{x^{\prime},y^{\prime},t^{\prime}\} such that deg⁡xi′=0,deg⁡yj′=−1,deg⁡t′=1\deg x^{\prime}_{i}=0,\deg y^{\prime}_{j}=-1,\deg t^{\prime}=1. Therefore the assertion is reduced to the divisor case for arbitrary mixed Hodge modules as above, and follows from the proof of Theorem 1.2. This completes the proof of Theorem 5.3.

For the moment, it is not clear whether the assertion of Theorem 5.3 holds under the assumption that TT is transversal to any stratum of a Whitney regular stratification of DD in the case DD is reduced.
